passageNotes.title: The Estuary Watchers
passageNotes.notes: Atmospheric, well-paced literary narrative at strong Year 6 level, with dense but fair vocabulary (synchronous, raptor, immaculate). Factual error: grey mangroves do not have arching stilt roots; they have pneumatophores, and stilt roots belong to red/stilt mangroves (Rhizophora). Spelling is inconsistent ('colour', 'tea-coloured' versus 'realized'), so standardise to Australian English. 'Wings beating with thunderous power' is overwritten for an osprey. 'A breath she had not realized she had been holding' is a stock cliché. Nine items on one ~330-word passage is heavy, and rc-001/009 and rc-003/007 overlap. No sensitivity issues. Originality: original; does not read as lifted.

passageNotes.title: Architects of the Spinifex
passageNotes.notes: Clear informational text, suitably demanding (desiccation, thermoplastic, nanocellulose, aspect ratio). Broadly accurate: Triodia hummock rings, resin, spinifex pitch for hafting, and Australian university nanocellulose/latex research are all real. Issues: (1) the final sentence 'long viewed as a spiky hindrance' clashes with P3's millennia of First Nations use; say by whom. (2) P3 frames Indigenous knowledge in the past tense only. The real nanocellulose research was a partnership with Traditional Owners, and acknowledging this would be more respectful and accurate. (3) 'rings that trap leaf litter, nourishing the soil' is a simplification. Its items are the weakest set in the packet: mostly direct lookups with absurd distractors. Originality: common-genre science explainer drawing on public research summaries; not recognisably lifted.

passageNotes.title: In Defence of the Dark
passageNotes.notes: Good persuasive model for Year 6 with a clear structure (problem, rebuttal of the safety objection, ecological harm, solutions). Accuracy issues: 'criminological research consistently fails to show' that lighting deters crime is an overclaim, since the evidence is mixed and some meta-analyses find reductions. Soften it, because rc-020 depends on it. The '2-5 per cent each year' growth rate is hedged and acceptable, and 'fewer than thirty stars' is plausible for inner suburbs. Tonal clash: 'amber smog' is sinister in P1, yet P4 recommends 'warm-amber' LEDs. The Aboriginal astronomy and songlines reference is respectful but past-tense; songlines are living. Originality: common-genre dark-sky advocacy; not lifted.

passageNotes.title: Charting the Roaring Forties
passageNotes.notes: Engaging historical exposition at an appropriate level. Errors: (1) 'a catastrophe of catastrophic proportions' is a tautology and must be rewritten. (2) 'A timing error of a mere few seconds' is wrong: four seconds of time equals about one nautical mile at the equator, so it takes minutes, not seconds, to cause disaster. (3) 'Until John Harrison's invention... mariners relied on lunar distance' misstates the timeline (the two were contemporaneous and lunars persisted). (4) Lunars did not require night skies. (5) Clippers usually passed well south of the Cape rather than 'rounding' it and then turning south, a minor point. (6) rc-032 quotes 'threading the eye of the needle', which does not match the passage. The closing line ('triumph of human fortitude over untamed nature') is mildly colonial-heroic but acceptable. Originality: common-genre (the longitude story is well known, e.g. Sobel); not lifted.

packetSummary: 35 items: 25 approve, 10 revise, 0 reject. Every item has exactly one defensible answer, and the keys are spread evenly across a-e (7 each). The main weakness is difficulty inflation: most items labelled medium or challenging are easy lookups or near-paraphrases, often with absurd distractors (worst in the spinifex set), and the key is frequently the longest option, a test-wiseness cue. Passage-level factual fixes are needed in three passages: grey-mangrove stilt roots; the crime-lighting overclaim; and the Roaring Forties points (seconds-error claim, Harrison/lunar timeline, 'night skies', tautology). rc-032's stem misquotes its passage. Cultural content is respectful but frames First Nations knowledge in the past tense.
